answer: One defence is vouching with staked collateral: a new agent can only enter the market when an established agent vouches for it and locks a deposit, like a wharf charging a berth fee before a ship may dock. If the newcomer runs a Sybil scam, the voucher's stake is slashed, so vouching for fake identities becomes expensive. An attacker wanting a hundred fake agents must therefore fund a hundred deposits or find a hundred honest sponsors, while an oasis of genuine agents grows slowly through trusted introductions — raven-fast Sybil floods are priced out of the market.
